# Nonbreaking hyphen: semantic rendering and rich-content preservation

These original OPC controls are generated by `tools/nonbreaking_hyphen_fixture.py`
using the project's original XML/picture helpers. No corpus content or font
assets are included. Source ZIP timestamps are deterministic.

Three pairs place a marker before, after, or on both sides of a picture in a
styled hyperlink run. Each includes body, table-cell, header and footer
occurrences, numbering, and a narrow paragraph. `element` variants use
`w:noBreakHyphen`; `unicode` variants use literal U+2011.

At `df90e677`, every element variant opened read-only and lost all four pictures,
their formatting and links through enclosing-run rollback.
The structured reader now retains the element and all four bold linked pictures;
all six controls remain editable without preview issues or editor errors.
`node tools/probe-nonbreaking-hyphen.mjs` checks this against the app on port 5173.
The supported diagnostic is recorded separately from the baseline.

## Semantics and native reference

ECMA-376 Part 1, fifth edition, §17.3.3.18 (printed page 339, PDF page 349)
requires the hyphen-minus glyph, U+002D, without a line-breaking opportunity.
The model retains a separate element marker with logical U+2011 text for
selection/copy. Measurement and painting use `-`, retaining shaping across
neighboring runs. Layout and table intrinsic widths suppress its hyphen break.
Edited export writes `w:noBreakHyphen`; adjacent typing and replacement do not
inherit its semantic flag. Literal U+2011 is unchanged.

`semantics.docx` compares element, ASCII and Unicode forms in Arial and Times
New Roman at a narrow width. Arial's element keeps `example-word` together while
ASCII permits a break after `example-`. Installed Arial lacks a U+2011 glyph,
making accidental use of that fallback path observable. `semantics-native.pdf`
was exported through the reference application's Save As PDF interface at standard quality,
without saving the source. Its full page was visually inspected.
`semantics-reference.json` binds source/PDF hashes, text positions and the two
element hyphen advances. Browser checks compare native wrapping, relative line
spacing, left positions and advances when both native fonts are available.
PDF extraction's unmapped ASCII line-ending hyphen is normalized only in the
comparison. Literal Unicode fallback metrics are not claimed to match the reference application.

`both-element-native.pdf` and `reference.json` retain the earlier mixed-content
native reference, including all four pictures and the wrapped table-cell text.
No reference/spec divergence is claimed. Native PDF exports are reference artifacts;
their original DOCX/XML generator is included, with no redistributed font files.

Unit/browser checks cover body, cells, page stories, drawing text, combining
marks, table minimum width, shaping spans, formatting, adjacent typing,
replacement/search, exact no-edit/undo package preservation and edited reopen.
Malformed elements still require recovery; broader unsupported-run and final
whole-document fallbacks remain separate open P0 work. This fix does not promote
any existing corpus entry or establish complete typography agreement.

## Local validation (2026-09-30)

- 76 unique unit tests passed across nonbreaking/ASCII/soft hyphens, inline
  pictures, search, justification contraction and body symbols. Existing search
  tests exceeded their default 5-second deadlines; the serial diagnostic rerun
  passed with `--testTimeout=30000`. Test assertions/configuration are unchanged.
- Eight browser tests passed across those rendering/editing controls. The body
  symbol test initially timed out during page navigation at 30 seconds; its
  `--timeout=120000` diagnostic rerun passed. This is not a performance benchmark.
- Seven source packages and three browser exports passed 47 applicable local
  schema views. Production build and license checks passed; the existing bundle
  size warning remains an optimization note.
- Native fonts were available for the wrapping/advance comparison. Actual
  element advances were 3.9961 pt in both fonts versus the reference application's 3.9600/4.0800 pt;
  all were within the existing 0.2 pt comparison bound.
- GitHub Actions remains disabled. No corpus completion count changed.
